# Chats

The main panel: the transcript as it reads, and the composer under it.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The tool call, the plus, the mode and the effort answer the pointer.

## The transcript

Prompts, replies, tool calls, thoughts and subagents, laid out like the Claude app. Your prompts sit in a bubble with a tail, replies run the width, and code blocks are colored with a copy button. A tool call is a card, its badge colored by what it does, and three or more in a row fold into one line with a tally. **Explain** puts one plain sentence on an opaque call, asked of the agent’s small model in a session of its own, so nothing of it enters yours.

While the agent works, approvals, questions and plans arrive as cards at the end, and anything the window has no card for shows on its terminal card. ⌘F finds in the chat; ⌘G steps to the next hit.

## The composer

Type and send: ↩︎ or ⌘↩︎, your choice, and ⇧↩︎ is a new line. A session running in a terminal gets the message through the agent’s inbox; a finished one resumes under Emaki. Drafts survive quitting.

- **Attach** by paste, drop or the **+** button. A picture shows as a thumbnail, any other file as a chip with its name and size.
- **`@`** picks a file or folder from the project, as the agent’s own prompt does.
- **`/`** lists the slash commands and skills the agent knows. A command that acts alone runs on ↩︎; a skill goes into the message.
- Spelling and grammar are checked as you type, with corrections on the right-click menu.

To talk instead of typing, in Emaki or any other app, there is [Kotoba](https://github.com/alkaline-software/kotoba), our dictation app for the Mac.

## Mode, model and effort

Three pills under the composer, in the agent’s own colors, each opening its list in place. ⇧Tab steps the mode, as it does in the terminal. A new session starts with the defaults set in Settings, New sessions; the pills change them for this one.

## The status bar

The row under the composer says how much of the context window is used and where the five-hour and seven-day limits stand, colored at the thresholds the agent’s own status line uses, for Claude Code and Codex alike. Notices land there too: what a command did, or why something could not be done.
